verdict.rationale: cubic documents real programmatic surfaces: an Analytics API with a published OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec, a Members API, and an official MCP server that can request PR reviews, triage scan issues, and manage subscription seats and roles. Nothing shows these cover the full UI, though; many UI-driven features have no documented API equivalent, and much configuration happens through cubic.yaml rather than an API. missing for 10: documented API endpoints for triggering reviews/Ultrareview, Fix with cubic, custom agents, auto-approval settings, codebase scans, wiki and cross-repo configuration, plus any explicit API–UI parity statement or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Analytics API gives you PR-level data on how many issues were flagged, how many were fixed, how much AI code was authored, etc.
Each Members API endpoint page's markdown mirror embeds the full OpenAPI 3.1.0 YAML for that operation
Connect cubic's MCP server to your coding agent to read review findings and codebase context, request PR reviews, and triage PR or codebase scan issues.
You can now ask your coding agent to check your cubic subscription, manage team seats and roles, and purchase more seats without leaving your MCP client.
